quick: Addison: 0.1 mg PO daily (range 0.1 mg 3x/wk to 0.2 mg daily)
May take with food to reduce GI upset
Use if clearly needed; category C - monitor
Caution; monitor BP, sodium, potassium, fluid status
Blood pressure, serum potassium and sodium, edema, weight
summary: Fludrocortisone acetate is a potent synthetic corticosteroid with marked mineralocorticoid (salt-retaining) and some glucocorticoid activity. At the small doses used (about 0.1 mg/day) it acts essentially as a mineralocorticoid for replacement in Addison disease and primary adrenocortical insufficiency, and for salt-losing congenital adrenal hyperplasia. It promotes sodium and water retention and potassium excretion, so blood pressure and serum potassium must be monitored; the main risks are hypertension, edema, hypokalemia and heart failure.
indications: Partial replacement therapy for primary and secondary adrenocortical insufficiency in Addison disease
Treatment of salt-losing forms of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (adrenogenital syndrome)

dosage.d: 0.1 mg daily (range 0.1 mg three times weekly to 0.2 mg daily)
dosage.n: Given with cortisone or hydrocortisone; titrate to BP, potassium and renin
With glucocorticoid; monitor electrolytes, renin and growth in children

admin: Take orally once daily, with food if it causes stomach upset
Use together with a glucocorticoid (hydrocortisone/cortisone) for full adrenal replacement
Ensure adequate dietary sodium; the dose may need adjusting in heat, illness or salt loss
Do not stop abruptly - taper under supervision to avoid adrenal crisis
Titrate to blood pressure, serum potassium, sodium and plasma renin activity
moa: Fludrocortisone is a 9-alpha-fluoro derivative of hydrocortisone. It binds the mineralocorticoid receptor in the distal renal tubule, promoting reabsorption of sodium (and water) and increasing urinary excretion of potassium and hydrogen ions. This restores sodium/volume status and blood pressure in adrenal insufficiency. It also has glucocorticoid activity, but the doses used for mineralocorticoid replacement are too small to provide meaningful glucocorticoid effect.

relative: Active or latent infections (immunosuppression), including untreated TB
monitor: Patients under physical stress (may need increased glucocorticoid, not mineralocorticoid)

preg: Fludrocortisone is pregnancy category C; corticosteroids can affect the fetus. Use only if clearly needed for adrenal replacement, at the lowest effective dose, and monitor mother and infant (including for hypoadrenalism in the neonate).
lact: Corticosteroids are excreted in human milk; use with caution during breastfeeding and observe the infant for any effects, though replacement doses are small.
renal: Use with caution; the salt- and water-retaining action can worsen hypertension, edema and cardiac load. Monitor blood pressure, serum sodium, potassium and fluid status closely.
hepatic: Use with caution; patients with cirrhosis show an enhanced effect of the drug, so lower doses may suffice and closer monitoring is needed.

major: Potassium-depleting agents (loop/thiazide diuretics, amphotericin B) - additive hypokalemia; monitor potassium
Drugs whose action is affected by potassium - e.g. digoxin toxicity is potentiated by hypokalemia
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (barbiturates, phenytoin, rifampin) - increase corticosteroid clearance and may reduce effect
Anticoagulants - corticosteroids may alter response; monitor
Vaccines - reduced response; avoid live vaccines if immunosuppressive doses
Antidiabetic agents - corticosteroid may raise glucose, reducing their effect
minor: Salicylates - corticosteroids increase clearance; watch for salicylate toxicity on withdrawal
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce GI upset; ensure adequate dietary salt as advised.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; increases gastrointestinal irritation and may affect blood pressure control.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes hypokalemia, sodium retention, possible hyperglycemia and metabolic alkalosis; may suppress reactions to skin tests.

serious: Severe hypokalemia with arrhythmia or muscle weakness
Growth suppression in children (with glucocorticoid effect)
rare: Adrenal suppression with abrupt withdrawal (adrenal crisis)
Increased susceptibility to or masking of infection
emergency: Acute adrenal crisis (on abrupt withdrawal or under-replacement during stress)
Acute pulmonary edema / decompensated heart failure

monitoring: Blood pressure regularly - reduce dose if hypertension develops
Serum potassium and sodium; watch for hypokalemia and fluid overload
Body weight and signs of edema
Plasma renin activity to guide adequacy of mineralocorticoid replacement
Growth and electrolytes in children with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and never stop suddenly - missing doses or stopping can trigger a dangerous adrenal crisis
Keep up the salt intake your doctor advises and report swelling, rapid weight gain, breathlessness or muscle weakness
Carry a steroid-dependency alert card and tell any treating clinician you take adrenal replacement
During illness, fever, surgery or injury, your glucocorticoid dose may need increasing - contact your care team
pk: Plasma peak ~1.7 hours after an oral dose
Plasma half-life ~3.5 hours; biological half-life 18-36 hours
Long biological action supports once-daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature, protect from light/moisture
pearls: Used as a mineralocorticoid: at ~0.1 mg/day the glucocorticoid effect is negligible, so it is given WITH hydrocortisone/cortisone for full adrenal replacement
Monitor blood pressure and serum potassium - salt/water retention causes hypertension and edema, and hypokalemia is common
Plasma renin activity helps titrate the dose - high renin suggests under-replacement, low/suppressed renin with hypertension suggests over-replacement
Stress doses: increase the glucocorticoid (not fludrocortisone) during illness, surgery or injury to prevent adrenal crisis
Cirrhosis enhances the effect - use lower doses and monitor closely
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Do not stop the medicine on your own; missed adrenal-replacement doses can lead to crisis, so contact your care team if doses are repeatedly missed.
overdose: Overdose or excessive dosing causes hypertension, edema, hypokalemia, weight gain and potentially heart failure. Stop or reduce the drug, restrict sodium, give potassium supplementation as needed, and provide supportive care; reduce the dose for transient hypertension.
